name: KnowYourRules controlled real-model evaluation cases
status: SYNTHETIC. Every passage is invented test text from eval/answer-quality/fixtures.json, not a Telangana legal provision. Expected behaviour is derived only from what each synthetic passage says. Results on these cases do not measure legal correctness on real Telangana provisions.

fictional_stamp_must.text: Synthetic Clause A, fictional test text. The keeper of a test registry shall stamp the test card in blue ink.
fictional_stamp_must.note: Fictional test text written for this evaluation. Not legislation and not representative of any law.

fictional_stamp_must_not.text: Synthetic Clause B, fictional test text. The keeper of a test registry shall not stamp the test card in blue ink.
fictional_stamp_must_not.note: Fictional test text written for this evaluation. Not legislation and not representative of any law.

sample_mock_responses_note: Hand-written illustrative responses used only for the sample report and mocked tests. They are not model output.

cases.question: Must the keeper of a test registry stamp the test card in blue ink?

expected.justification: Fictional pair: E1 and E2 have the same actor (the keeper of a test registry), the same action and object (stamp the test card in blue ink) and no condition or scope limit; E1 requires it and E2 prohibits it, and neither says it prevails. The instructions (rule 9) require 'conflicting', one claim per side citing its own passage; an answer that picks one side is not acceptable.

claims.text: The keeper of a test registry shall stamp the test card in blue ink.

claims.text: The keeper of a test registry shall stamp the test card in blue ink.
The keeper of a test registry shall not stamp the test card in blue ink.

cases.question: Must riders wear helmets on rural roads?

expected.justification: E2 is the passage on rural roads (an exemption); E1 is the general duty. An answer must state the E2 exemption; citing E1 as well is permitted, not required.

sample_mock_responses.answer: Every rider of a two-wheeler shall wear protective headgear, except a person exempted under sub-rule (2). (2) A Sikh wearing a turban is exempted. Riders on rural roads are exempt from protective headgear.

claims.text: Every rider of a two-wheeler shall wear protective headgear, except a person exempted under sub-rule (2). (2) A Sikh wearing a turban is exempted.
Riders on rural roads are exempt from protective headgear.

cases.question: Is protective headgear compulsory for every rider of a two-wheeler?

expected.justification: E1 states the duty with its own exception (a Sikh wearing a turban); E2 exempts riders on rural roads, which qualifies 'every rider'. A complete answer keeps the E1 exception and cites the E2 exemption.

cases.question: Can a learner drive a motor car?

expected.justification: E1 permits it only with the proviso that a licensed instructor sits beside the learner (instructions rule 4).

sample_mock_responses.answer: A learner may drive a motor car, provided that a licensed instructor sits beside the learner.

claims.text: A learner may drive a motor car, provided that a licensed instructor sits beside the learner.

cases.question: Can a learner drive a motor car on a national highway?

required_phrases.text: not drive on a national highway

expected.justification: E2 opens 'Notwithstanding anything in rule 305', so the synthetic text itself says E2 prevails over E1 for national highways: the passages do not conflict. Only an answer that states the E2 prohibition and cites E2 is acceptable; a 'conflicting' response, or one that omits the prohibition, ignores the override.

sample_mock_responses.answer: A learner may drive a motor car, provided that a licensed instructor sits beside the learner. Notwithstanding anything in rule 305, a learner shall not drive on a national highway.

claims.text: A learner may drive a motor car, provided that a licensed instructor sits beside the learner.
Notwithstanding anything in rule 305, a learner shall not drive on a national highway.

cases.question: Can a school bus carry standing passengers?

expected.justification: E1 permits standing passengers only when all seats are occupied; dropping that condition changes the rule.

sample_mock_responses.answer: A school bus may carry standing passengers.

claims.text: A school bus may carry standing passengers.

cases.question: Can a goods vehicle carry passengers?

expected.justification: E1 prohibits passengers except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods.

sample_mock_responses.answer: A goods vehicle shall not carry passengers, except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods.

claims.text: A goods vehicle shall not carry passengers, except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods.

cases.question: Can a goods vehicle carry people?

expected.justification: E1 prohibits passengers except the owner or hirer; E2 permits farm labourers with the goods. Both bear on 'people', so both must be cited.

sample_mock_responses.answer: A goods vehicle shall not carry passengers, except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods.

claims.text: A goods vehicle shall not carry passengers, except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods.

sample_mock_responses.answer: A goods vehicle shall not carry passengers, except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods. A goods vehicle may carry farm labourers with the goods.

claims.text: A goods vehicle shall not carry passengers, except the owner or hirer travelling with the goods.
A goods vehicle may carry farm labourers with the goods.

phrase_kinds.condition: an exception, proviso, condition or restriction that the source passage attaches to its statement ("except ...", "provided that ...", "only when / only to ..."); dropping it changes the rule
phrase_kinds.content: the position a passage states (who, what action, what object, which modality or scope); it must appear for the answer to state that passage's position at all
